clips.title: Temporal Explained • Determinism
clips.why: Why Temporal needs workflow code to make the same decisions on every replay, and how it uses the history to check that.
look: Why replay can only work if the code asks for the same steps as before.
How Temporal notices code that no longer matches what happened.
clips.after: A deploy that adds a step changes the code under a recorded history, which is exactly the mismatch this clip describes.

clips.title: Move Fast WITHOUT Breaking Anything - Workflow Versioning with Temporal
clips.why: The idea behind patched, explained by Temporal: you do not version the whole workflow, you mark each change with a change ID.
look: A change ID in the code, and the history remembers which side of it a run took.
He uses the Go SDK's GetVersion; patched is the TypeScript form of the same idea.
clips.after: grill-step is our change ID: runs from before the deploy replay the old path, and runs after it take the new one.

clips.title: Temporal & AI | Agent Memory & State
clips.why: A short explanation of why histories have limits, and the two ways around them, one of which is Continue-As-New.
look: Why an agent loop that runs for a long time grows a long history.
Continue-As-New: a fresh history that continues with the state you give it.
clips.after: Our slots workflow never ends, so it continues as new after 5,000 events and passes its holders and waiting line along.

practice.q: Which of these changes to ticketToPr needs a patch, if runs are open?

options.text: Moving the reminder before the plan is posted
options.why: That reorders a timer and an activity, so an open run's history would no longer match the code.

options.text: Fixing a typo in the Slack message that the notify activity posts
options.why: The message is built inside the activity. Activity code is never replayed.

options.text: Adding a comment above the signal handlers
options.why: Comments and names are not commands. Replay only compares commands with the history.

practice.q: Wrap the new grill step so runs that started before the deploy skip it.
practice.hint: It comes from @temporalio/workflow and returns true or false, based on a marker in the history.
practice.why: patched returns true for runs that reach the line after the deploy, and false when replaying an older history without the marker.

practice.q: Put the life of the grill-step patch in order.
items: Deploy 1 wraps the grill in if (patched("grill-step"))
Runs that started before deploy 1 replay without the grill and finish on the old path
A list query shows no open run that started before deploy 1
Deploy 2 replaces the check with deprecatePatch("grill-step") and a plain grill call
When no run from before deploy 2 is open, deploy 3 deletes the deprecatePatch line
practice.why: Each step waits until the runs that need the previous code are closed. A replay test in CI catches a step taken too early.

practice.q: slots has handed out slots for weeks. Finish the last line so it starts a fresh history and keeps its state.
practice.hint: It continues the same workflow ID as a new run.
practice.why: continueAsNew ends this run and starts a new one with an empty history. Only the arguments carry over, so the holders and the waiting line must be passed.

practice.q: After a careless deploy, the worker logs a non-determinism error for nova:RH-1234. What is the state of the run?

options.text: Failed, and the ticket must be assigned again
options.why: The run does not fail. It waits for code that matches its history.

options.text: Open, but stuck: the worker retries it and fails each time until compatible code is deployed
options.why: That is why the fix is in the code. Deploy a patched version and the run continues where it stopped.

options.text: Completed, but without the new step
options.why: Nothing moves while the code and the history disagree.
